papers.title: Long-term outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stents versus coronary artery bypass grafting for left main coronary artery disease: a prospective analysis of the multicentre IRIS-MAIN registry.
papers.summary: In the multicentre IRIS-MAIN registry of Asian patients with unprotected left main disease, 5,379 underwent revascularisation with drug-eluting-stent PCI (n=3,836) or CABG (n=1,543) and were followed for a median 10.0 years. In the propensity overlap-weighted analysis, 10-year all-cause mortality was 24.0% after PCI versus 22.9% after CABG (overlap-weighted HR 1.00, 95% CI 0.87–1.14; P=0.99). The confidence interval does not exclude benefit or harm with either strategy; the authors stress these observational findings cannot establish causal equivalence.
papers.study_type: Prospective multicentre registry with target-trial emulation
papers.short_title: long-term PCI versus CABG for left main disease in IRIS-MAIN

papers.title: Efficacy and Safety of Routine Postdilation in Balloon-Expandable Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation Platform: The DUOTAP Randomized Clinical Trial.
papers.summary: In this randomised trial of 148 patients undergoing balloon-expandable TAVI (median age 81 years), routine postdilation with the delivery balloon versus sham/no postdilation cut the fluoroscopic THV asymmetry index by 70% (median 1.2% vs 2.8%; geometric mean ratio 0.30; 95% CI 0.18–0.47; P<0.001). Postdilation also enlarged CT-derived valve areas at inflow, midframe and outflow, reduced hypoattenuated leaflet thickening and mild-or-worse paravalvular leak, and raised the Doppler Velocity Index, without increasing procedure-related adverse events (P=0.36).

papers.title: Effectiveness of Radiofrequency Renal Denervation in the United States: Six-Month Primary End Point Results From the SPYRAL AFFIRM Study.
papers.summary: SPYRAL AFFIRM treated 594 US patients with uncontrolled hypertension using radiofrequency renal denervation (baseline office BP 169/106 mm Hg; mean 3.6 antihypertensives unchanged through 6 months). At 6 months, systolic BP fell by 18.2 mm Hg office, 9.4 mm Hg home and 9.7 mm Hg on 24-hour ambulatory monitoring (all P<0.001 vs baseline), meeting the primary performance goal of a −6.0 mm Hg office SBP change. Adverse clinical events through 6 months were uncommon.
papers.short_title: six-month US results of radiofrequency renal denervation in SPYRAL AFFIRM

papers.title: Prediction of Bailout Mechanical Circulatory Support Use for Hemodynamic Collapse During PCI: The ORACLE Score.
papers.summary: From 6,931 PCIs at a tertiary centre (bailout MCS for hemodynamic collapse 1.4%) and external validation in 214,877 BMC2 PCIs, six variables—non-elective presentation, systolic blood pressure, chronic heart failure, prior PCI, rotational/orbital atherectomy and left main PCI—predicted bailout MCS. The simplified ORACLE integer score kept most discrimination (AUC 0.791 derivation, 0.718 external) and stratified observed bailout rates from 0.4% (low risk) to 8.7% (high risk), with negative predictive value above 99% in both cohorts.
papers.study_type: Risk score derivation and external validation
papers.short_title: ORACLE score for bailout mechanical circulatory support during PCI

papers.title: Prognostic value of Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio after percutaneous coronary intervention.
papers.summary: In a FAVOR III China subgroup, offline post-PCI μQFR was analysed in 4,196 vessels from 3,455 patients. Five-year MACE was 23.1%, 19.0% and 17.2% across low, intermediate and high μQFR tertiles (P=0.001); versus μQFR >0.95, the lowest tertile (≤0.91) had adjusted HR 1.30 (95% CI 1.06–1.60). Using a ROC-derived cutoff, μQFR <0.94 versus ≥0.94 carried adjusted HR 1.23 (1.04–1.47), with no significant treatment-by-μQFR interaction (P=0.23).
papers.study_type: Prespecified subgroup analysis of a randomised trial
papers.short_title: prognostic value of post-PCI Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio

papers.title: Guided P2Y12 inhibitor selection after rapid CYP2C19 genotyping in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention.
papers.summary: Among 974 real-world PCI patients with rapid CYP2C19 genotyping, clopidogrel was prescribed at discharge more often in non-loss-of-function than loss-of-function carriers (43% vs 31%; P<0.001). After LOF stratification and confounder adjustment, major atherothrombotic events did not differ significantly between prasugrel/ticagrelor and clopidogrel (LOF adjusted HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.36–2.10; non-LOF 1.26, 0.67–2.36), and BARC bleeding was similar; the authors urge cautious interpretation.
papers.short_title: rapid CYP2C19 genotyping to guide P2Y12 inhibitor choice after PCI

papers.title: Prediction of coronary events by computed tomography-derived Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio.
papers.summary: In 885 vessels from 312 patients who had CCTA 6 months to 3 years before invasive angiography, CT-μFR ≤0.80 predicted higher 3-year vessel-level myocardial infarction or urgent ACS revascularisation (adjusted HR 6.87, 95% CI 5.26–8.96). Even when CT-μFR was >0.80, a CT-μFR gradient ≥0.004/mm remained associated with events (adjusted HR 2.59, 95% CI 1.63–4.11), and combining both improved the C-index from 0.575 to 0.655.
papers.short_title: CT-derived μQFR and pressure gradient for predicting coronary events

papers.title: Accuracy of Virtual Circle Method and Valve-to-Aorta Distance Change After Redo-TAVR: Multicenter Paired CT Analysis.
papers.summary: In 58 Redo-TAVR patients with paired pre- and post-procedural CT across Evolut-in-SAPIEN, SAPIEN-in-SAPIEN and SAPIEN-in-Evolut combinations, the virtual circle method predicted index TAV frame diameter within ±1 mm in 31 of 53 applicable cases (58.5%), overestimated in 26.4% and underestimated in 15.1%. Accurate or conservative estimates covered 85%; underestimation (median 1.3 mm) clustered where pre- and postdilatation were used.
papers.short_title: accuracy of the virtual circle method for Redo-TAVR planning

papers.title: Long-Term Impact of Vutrisiran in Patients With TTR Amyloidosis With Cardiomyopathy: 1-Year Efficacy and Safety Outcomes From the HELIOS-B Open-Label Extension.
papers.summary: In HELIOS-B's open-label extension (466 patients), continuous vutrisiran through month 48 reduced cardiovascular events or death by 37% versus delayed start after placebo (HR 0.63), with matching mortality benefit, higher KCCQ-OS (difference 9.0), more stable or improved NYHA class, and lower NT-proBNP and troponin I, without new safety signals.
papers.study_type: Open-label extension of a randomised trial
papers.short_title: long-term vutrisiran in TTR amyloid cardiomyopathy from the HELIOS-B extension

papers.title: Targeting ALDOA Lactylation Reverses Vascular Remodeling in Pulmonary Hypertension by Disrupting Actin Polymerization and YAP Activation.
papers.summary: In pulmonary hypertension models and human tissue, AARS1-driven ALDOA lysine-42 lactylation enhanced γ-actin binding, F-actin polymerization and YAP activation independent of glycolysis, driving pulmonary arterial smooth-muscle proliferation. Knockout or lactylation-deficient ALDOA, β-alanine, or raltegravir disrupting the ALDOA–γ-actin interaction attenuated experimental pulmonary hypertension and vascular remodeling.
papers.short_title: ALDOA lactylation and vascular remodeling in pulmonary hypertension
